scope: Critical original-primary research review of evolution of newly accessible aerobic citrate utilization, genotype-dependent fitness, narrow observed reversion with selection withdrawal, and imperfect niche maintenance; research only

sources.citation: Van Hofwegen DJ, Hovde CJ, Minnich SA. Rapid Evolution of Citrate Utilization by Escherichia coli by Direct Selection Requires citT and dctA. Journal of Bacteriology 198:1022-1034 (2016).
sources.rights: © 2016 American Society for Microbiology, All Rights Reserved, original paper accessible but no verified general CC redistribution license; only independent critical paraphrase and link
sources.grade: E2 publisher original complete main Results, Methods, Discussion and negative controls; supplements and original sequencing not independently reproduced
sources.program: University of Idaho group, genuinely distinct research laboratory from LTEE, but studies same metabolic capability in altered selection schedule
positive: Selection imposed with citrate sole or dominant resource produced rapidly appearing citrate-using E coli colonies in several strain backgrounds; phenotypic mutant isolates are not independent gene-origin lineages
Co-opted and amplified CitT preexisting anaerobic transporter expression with promoter rearrangement; DctA-associated refinement
Citrate growth confirmed using independent phenotype readouts and culture-metabolite assays
Same kind of new whole-cell aerobic metabolic ability obtained in independent lab with markedly different direct-selection interval
negative: citT deletion did not yield Cit-positive isolates in tested selection conditions
dctA deletion negative in short comparisons but one isolate SO191 recovered after 134 days; do not claim universal absolute requirement
Low-citrate selection yielded only 4/12 and 6/12 positive flasks for some E coli B backgrounds, not universal rapid origin
Initial weak variants could show extensive lag and altered cell morphology; morphologies were reversible in rich medium
No registered stable maintenance after complete removal of directed citrate selection or operator culture passages, and 46 isolates not whole-genome sequenced
sources.unit: Independent culture-origin mutants conditional on experimental flasks; DNA sequence analyses of four representatives; no independent abiotic origins

sources.citation: Leon D, D'Alton S, Quandt EM, Barrick JE. Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides. PLOS Genetics 14:e1007348 (2018).
sources.rights: CC BY 4.0 original journal article; no copied figures, gene sequence, supplementary contents or long excerpts
sources.grade: E2 publisher original full Methods/Results/Discussion, figure text, reported statistical units, disclosure and rights; no separate source/raw-sequence reanalysis
sources.program: University of Texas at Austin/Barrick, affiliated with Lenski LTEE original archive program; linked ancestry to 2020 and Pass9 citrate
positive: Single engineered activated-CitT cassette compared with null matched construct in time-series archival genotypes from one evolving LTEE population
Report modest about 2.2% advantage for authentic weak Cit+ duplication in early sampled background
Some background-specific functional modules produced significant competitive benefit, showing novel capability can be individually advantageous
Physically generated an original early Cit-positive clone's Cit-negative revertant after citrate-free passage and spontaneous collapse of duplicated regulatory module
negative: Some reconstructed backgrounds yielded marked costs: 11 report-negative backgrounds, five with >20% relative competitive penalty
The same functional module is not uniformly adaptive; strongly negative background strains increased growth lag even if culture could reach higher final density
23 additional background clones from one ancestral population are not independently evolved Cit+ origin events

Reported classifications: four benefited, nine nonsignificant, eleven harmed, which add to 24; authors reference 23 additional backgrounds; exact exclusive membership remains unverified; cannot silently normalize category counts
Reversion during citrate-free passage is a single identified comparison, not a selection-withdrawal cohort survival frequency
sources.unreconciled_category_arithmetic: 4+9+11=24 vs 23 additional tested; could include separate control/overlap/different one-vs-two-tail tests, but explanation unverified without individual-level original data reconstruction
sources.unit: 23 additional archived, related genetic backgrounds, matched comparisons, one naturally evolved Cit+ original and revertant; marker/control technical fitness replicates not evolutionary founders

sources.citation: Blount ZD, Maddamsetti R, Grant NA et al. Genomic and phenotypic evolution of Escherichia coli in a novel citrate-only resource environment. eLife 9:e55414 (2020).
sources.rights: CC BY 4.0 original eLife article, third-party work separate; critical paraphrase only
sources.grade: E2-partial original indexed Methods/Results/figure text plus author/reviewer exchanges; direct full continuous publisher opening client-challenged; no full supplements/raw sequencing independent reanalysis
sources.program: Lenski/Barrick collaborator group, dependent on original Ara-3 LTEE Cit+ ancestors, NOT independent new Cit+ origin
sources.founders: Three Cit+ clones from generation 33,000 of a single Ara-3 LTEE lineage plus three isogenic arabinose-marker revertant descendants (all Cit-positive at start)
positive: Population-level citrate-only growth curves generally evolved reduced lag time and higher growth rates under managed passage
Structural variation including insertion sequences and gene amplification among evolved descendants, suggesting within-niche adaptation
Screened 24 lines for sequence changes after maintained laboratory evolution, a follow-up study of an inherited functional innovation
negative: Some evolved clones/populations appeared to decline in competition fitness despite sustained laboratory propagation, growth assays not equivalent to death-rate assays
Five examined microscope clone backgrounds, not all 24 evolved populations, supplied substantial clone-specific stationary-phase death-stain observations and admitted replication limits
A Cit-negative clone ZDBp874 lacking CitT genomic amplification recovered from one DM0-evolved population; second clone ZDBp875 from same population was Cit-positive
Phenotypic screens of hundreds of other clones from DM0-2 found no additional Cit-negative variant; single loss is consistent with transient reversion or rare coexisting lineage, not population loss
Continued manual culture and relevant citrate availability: no multi-founder selection-withdrawal persistence test
sources.staining_scope: five clone identities with nested imaging fields/cells and limited culture replicates; no 24-population-level death rates; potential phase/timing confounds and peer-review limitations noted

independence.independent_new_origin_programs: Idaho Van Hofwegen (2016) independent direct-selection study vs Lenski original evolution program; 2018 and 2020 compare/re-use descendants of one 1988 LTEE origin with overlapping researchers
independence.difference_in_selection_environment: 2016 explicitly lengthy direct citrate selection vs ancestral LTEE daily glucose-advantaged transfer; 2020 trials begin with already Cit-positive ancestors

release_gate: Require successful offline CI at exact PR head, unchanged main and reviewed PR head immediately prior to expected-head merge; independent post-merge main push CI success required for verified publication.
